Start here

Use the button above to open your workspace. It holds six small bit manipulation problems, and each one has its
own folder and files.

Problems

Expand each problem below to read it. All six must pass to earn full credit.

Problem 1: Keep the Low Half

Location: problem1/low_half.c

The file low_half.c already has a main that reads numbers, hands each one to low_half
and prints what comes back.

What to do

Write low_half as the title describes. Use bitwise operators only:
no loops, no arrays and no library calls.

Examples

Input: 0xb2be1200
Output: 0x1657c

Input: 0x6832a200
Output: 0x34195100

Input: 0x13a1b280
Output: 0x2743650

Input: 0x8843ad80
Output: 0x4421d6c

Input: 0xa5b1a000
Output: 0x14b6340

Input: 0x6d83e000
Output: 0x36c1f000

Input: 0x5d402080
Output: 0x17500

Input: 0xde1c5e00
Output: 0x1bc38

Input: 0x397ce00
Output: 0x1cbe700

Hints

Use a mask to keep only the bits you need. A shift by 10 moves the part you want down to the lowest position.
Remember that the right shift of a signed value may copy the sign bit, so declare your variables as unsigned.

Testing

Compile with make low_half and run the program. Try the examples above, then try zero, the largest 32-bit value and a value with only the top bit set.
Run the autograder from the workspace to check all of your problems at once.

Output: 0x1fe21300

Output: 0x26a7

Run the autograder from the workspace to check all of your problems at once.

Submission

Save every file in the workspace and press Submit. You can resubmit as many times as you like before the deadline.
Make sure that each problem passes the autograder, because partial credit is not given for a problem that fails any test.
